newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols inch up after auction.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols inch up after auction.

text.p: Implied volatilities for debt options inched up after poor results in the Treasury's 10-year note auction and mixed readings in the Federal Reserve's Beige Book report, traders said.
Still, the underlying markets appeared to find support at lower levels, and time-decay worries dampened the pickup in option pricing levels, they added.

"We're certainly seeing volatility buying, but the thing is, it's not going anywhere," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). "People have not made money being long options this year."
Traders said there was good interest to buy slightly out-of-the-money September 93.75 puts, December 93.50 puts and short-June 93.25 puts.
Volatilities for September and December CME Eurodollar futures options stood at 9.4/9.7 and 11.0/11.2 percent respectively, up 0.1 to 0.2 point each.

In short-June options, the so-called mid-curve options which expire next month but are priced off June 1998 futures, 93.00/93.25 bear put spread continued to be a very popular strategy as the market awaited the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, traders said.
June 1998 futures were off seven basis points at 93.36.

"If you have any idea that the Fed is going to tighten, I think the market (futures) is pretty expensive," the CME trader said, adding that Eurodollar futures could slide further ahead of the FOMC meeting.

Still, he added that implied volatilities could stay subdued even if such slides did occur because there seemed to be growing complacency that even if the Fed did raise rates, that might be the last tightening of the cycle.
"Until we see a surprise, vols are going to have a hard time going up," he said.
In Treasury bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade, traders said there had been sporadic put buying earlier in the day but activity tapered off toward the release of the auction results.
Implied volatility for June T-bond futures options stood at around 7.9 percent, up a quarter point on the day.
"On the whole, it's been a relatively quiet day in options," a brokerage firm trader at the CBOT said. "We have been just chopping around in this area (mid- to low-109s in June futures)."
June futures had been down about half a point for most of the day and slid another quarter point or so after the auction results to a low of 109-8/32.
The 10-year note auction, which came on the heels of Tuesday's sloppy three-year note auction, produced an average yield of 6.740 percent and a low bid-to-cover ratio of 1.86.

Traders said the market's next big event would be Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech in New York Thursday evening. They said Greenspan's remarks needed close watching because the Fed's March tightening had been preceded by surprisingly clear warnings from him.
